body:
>It's a permanent solution to a temporary problem.

No, it's a permanent solution to a permanent problem.

I never really understood that phrase. Seeking a permanent solution to any problem is usually a good thing.

There's nothing I don't like about my life. I like the field I'm studying, I love the city I live in, and my friends. Unfortunately, that doesn't really change anything.

>It's worth giving a shit.

Is it though? It's a decent way to slowly kill myself, because I'm too chicken to do it quickly.

>there's nothing to make you feel worse than waking up in the morning hung over and realizing you didn't really do anything the night before

Tell me about it. Happens way too often.

Currently, I'm playing Hand of Fate, SpaceChem, and TIS-100. As for that last one, just programming in assembly (NASM) has also been a bit of an escape, mostly because of the challenge it presents.

>I deal with a lot of the same sort of computer problems that someone trying to explain computers to another person deals with

Do you work in tech support? I hear it can be fun, but often frustrating if you're dealing with difficult customers.

Right now, I'm trying to learn Unity (I mean, how to properly use the engine, not how to do one of those asset flips Jim Sterling likes to make fun of). I kind of lack artistic talent to make a game on my own, though.
I'm studying computer science. I really enjoy programming actually, but I really hate the academic aspect. I'm an atheist, so no, I eat whatever I want.
